Buying a stock after a one-day 26% move with RSI above 70 is exactly the kind of FOMO the rules were designed to prevent. WHAT FAILED: This is now four trading days without a single execution. MU was queued yesterday as a BUY signal — the first qualifying setup since simulator launch — and it appears it did not execute today. The ceasefire collapse changed the macro picture overnight, which may have invalidated the MU thesis (semiconductor demand tied to global trade stability). But this pattern of finding one qualifying trade and then having the macro shift negate it before execution is a real risk to the strategy. If the system consistently identifies setups on Day N that are invalidated by Day N+1, we will never deploy capital. The execution pipeline needs review — specifically, should qualifying BUY signals trigger same-day limit orders rather than next-day market orders? That is a process improvement to consider.

WAS MORNING BRIEF SENTIMENT ACCURATE? Yes. The trade_decision correctly identified ceasefire collapse as a source of high uncertainty and the CPI print tomorrow as an additional reason to stay defensive. The macro read was accurate — this was not a day to be aggressive. Energy names in SELL territory, defense names with bearish patterns (H&S), and the only momentum play (INTC) was overbought. The brief saw the landscape clearly.

LESSONS LEARNED: (1) Four days of cash preservation is not failure when the market provides zero qualifying setups. But it does raise the question: are the criteria too strict for a paper trading simulator? In real capital, this conservatism is a virtue. In a learning environment, the absence of any trades means the system is generating no data on execution, position management, or exit discipline. (2) The ceasefire-to-collapse cycle in 24 hours (April 8 ceasefire → April 9 collapse) vindicates the small position sizing rule. Had we entered MU at 10 yesterday and the macro shifted overnight, the 8% stop would have been our only protection. (3) INTC at RSI 72 post-Terafab is worth watching for a pullback to the 50-60 RSI range — if the AI chip thesis remains intact, a consolidation entry could be strong. (4) The CPI print tomorrow is the next binary catalyst. Stay flat into it.

WHAT TO WATCH TOMORROW (Friday, Apr 10): CPI is the headline event. Three scenarios: (A) CPI comes in hot — Fed stays hawkish, growth/tech sells off, defensive positioning preferred. Watch for TLT short or UNH (healthcare is CPI-defensive). (B) CPI comes in cool — risk-on rally, AVGO and INTC benefit, consider AVGO if it clears BUY threshold. (C) CPI in-line — market likely flat, look for individual stock catalysts. Regardless of CPI: INTC pullback to RSI 55-60 range is the top watchlist item. UNH remains the scenario-neutral play with the MA rate catalyst. Energy (XOM, CVX) — avoid until oil finds a floor. Defense (LMT, RTX) — bearish patterns need to resolve before entry. Patience continues to be the edge, but we need to be ready to act when the first post-CPI qualifying setup appears.
